title: Avincis surpasses 9,200 firefighting flight hours across Spain, Portugal and Italy
summary: Firefighting flight hours have increased by nearly 90% compared with the same period last year, Avincis said.
body_text: Avincis, Europe’s largest aerial emergency services operator, has completed more than 9,200 flight hours and nearly 3,900 firefighting missions across Spain, Portugal and Italy during the 2026 wildfire season. To put these figures into context, Avincis’ firefighting flight hours across Spain, Portugal and Italy have increased by nearly 90 % compared with the same period last year. In the process, its crews have dropped nearly 200 million liters of water—enough to fill nearly 80 Olympic-sized swimming pools. Together, these figures reflect the scale of one of Europe’s most challenging wildfire seasons in recent years and the growing demand placed on aerial firefighting operations across the continent. As wildfire seasons become longer and more intense, Avincis is structured to provide a scalable aerial emergency response across Europe. The company continues to work closely with public authorities, civil protection bodies, fire and rescue services and other emergency organizations across Southern Europe. Globally, the company operates a firefighting fleet of around 70 aircraft, including 22 Canadair water bombers, enabling it to reinforce firefighting operations in Southern Europe as demand peaks throughout the season. Across Spain, Portugal and Italy, Avincis operates a fully integrated response model, with pilots, engineers, maintenance technicians, operational teams and support personnel working together to keep aircraft mission-ready. From planning and maintenance to deployment and recovery, every mission is coordinated to ensure a safe, reliable and continuous response. John Boag, Group CEO of Avincis, said: “Wildfire seasons are becoming longer, and the pressure is being felt across the industry. Aircraft that once operated for three or four months during the summer are now required from as early as March through to October. This makes it more difficult to move aircraft and crews between regions, recruit experienced pilots and plan for a season that no longer has a clearly defined end point. “Meeting this demand is not only about aircraft—it is about people. Our focus is on training our crews throughout the year and ensuring close coordination between firefighters on the ground and pilots in the air. That teamwork is what makes the difference when a fire breaks out.” Spain and Portugal So far this season, Avincis has logged 5,630 flight hours and 2,533 missions, dropping more than 120 million litres of water across the Iberian Peninsula. Across the region, the company is currently operating 52 aircraft — a mixed fleet including the Canadair CL-215, Airbus AS332, Airbus AS350, Airbus AS355 , Bell 212 , Bell 407 , Bell 412— supported by 266 professionals working across flight operations, engineering, maintenance and other technical and operational functions. This combination of amphibious water bombers and different helicopter types give the operation the flexibility to manage crew rotations, scheduled inspections and maintenance requirements, while maintaining the level of aircraft availability required during periods of intense activity. This press release was prepared and distributed by Avincis.

title: Freenow by Lyft and Baidu start AV testing in London
summary: Freenow by Lyft and Baidu's Apollo Go begin autonomous vehicle testing in London with RT6s. Research shows 58% of Londoners would try autonomous rides.
body_text: Research shows strong appetite for AVs among Londoners: over half say they’d likely ride in an autonomous vehicle and nearly two-thirds of those under 35 are in support of AVs being available in the capital Apollo Go's sixth-generation autonomous vehicles (RT6) are purpose-built for ride-hailing with advanced driverless technology London, 28 July 2026 - Freenow by Lyft and Baidu’s Apollo Go have officially commenced testing the sixth-generation autonomous vehicles from Apollo Go in London. The vehicles have safety operators and to start with will operate within the borough of Brent, which has a mix of urban and suburban environments. This builds on Lyft's 2025 announcement with Baidu for European deployment. Safety and close collaboration with city officials are central to this programme. Freenow and Lyft have been in extensive discussions with Transport for London (TfL) and the Centre for Connected and Autonomous Vehicles (CCAV), aligning with regulators to support a safe, reliable and sustainable service for Londoners. Thomas Zimmermann, CEO of Freenow by Lyft, said: "As a platform with deep roots in the taxi industry, our priority is ensuring that autonomous technology supports the professional drivers who keep London moving. By integrating these purpose-built, autonomous vehicles from Baidu’s Apollo Go into the Freenow by Lyft ecosystem, we will give Londoners more sustainable choices to travel, encouraging them to choose shared mobility services over personally-owned vehicles." The vehicles will operate as part of a hybrid network, with both Freenow’s established taxi and private hire vehicles and AVs. For riders, this will mean faster pickup times as the number of vehicles on the platform increases. "The arrival of Apollo Go vehicles in London marks a defining milestone in our global expansion," said Nan Yang, Vice President of Baidu and General Manager of Overseas Business Unit, Intelligent Driving Group . "Testing our autonomous fleet in one of the world’s most iconic and complex urban environments validates our technology’s maturity and our commitment to this market. By combining our cutting-edge autonomous driving technology with Freenow by Lyft’s local operational expertise, we are officially moving from vision to reality, together.” Recent research by Censuswide* reveals strong early interest in autonomous vehicles among Londoners, despite limited first-hand experience: 48% have never ridden one, yet 58% say they'd be likely to try it. Support is even higher among younger Londoners, with nearly two-thirds of those under 35 in favor of AVs being available in the capital. A further 25% said they're excited about having another transport option to choose from. Asked why they'd choose an AV, over half (51%) cited excitement about the technology, 43% pointed to reliability, and 41% said they'd value the opportunity for quiet "me time" during their journey. Freenow by Lyft and Baidu’s Apollo Go will welcome public riders in these vehicles starting in 2027. *This research was commissioned by Freenow by Lyft in partnership with Censuswide in March 2026. The survey sampled 3,001 respondents. About Freenow by Lyft Freenow by Lyft features broad multi-mobility options across 9 European markets and over 180 cities. Millions of passengers can access various mobility services within a single app, including taxis, private hire vehicles, carsharing, car rental, e-scooters, e-bikes, e-mopeds and public transport. With headquarters in Hamburg, Germany, Freenow is led by CEO Thomas Zimmermann. In July 2025, Freenow was acquired by Lyft, a global mobility platform offering a mix of rideshare, taxis, private hire vehicles, executive chauffeur services, car sharing, bikes, and scooters across 6 continents and thousands of cities. Millions of drivers have chosen to earn on billions of rides. Together, Freenow and Lyft are helping to create a more connected world, with transportation options for everyone.
